# Verbs

A verb is what an effect calls: `{ "damage": { "at": "here", … } }` (05 §10.1, §10.7). Its arguments are given by name, each an expression of the declared type; one marked *direct* may be given alone. A verb that declines gives a [reason](reasons.md) and the rule carries on. The console offers every verb as a command (14 §3.3). Rules with parameters that mods define are verbs too, under their qualified ids. The effects of the rule system itself are on the [effects](effects.md) page.

<a id="add-field"></a>
## `add_field`

Adds to the level of a field in a cell, or takes from it (02 §16), between 0 and 255. Raises `field_appeared` or `field_vanished` when the field comes or goes. Returns the level it had. Refused for a cell not loaded and a field that does not exist.

- `at` (loc): The cell.
- `field` (id<field>): The field.
- `amount` (int): How much to add; less than zero takes away.

<a id="add-modifier"></a>
## `add_modifier`

Adds a modifier to an attribute under a key (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `attr` (id<attribute>): Which attribute.
- `key` (string): The name it is added under and removed by.
- `add` (number, optional): Added to the base. Left out, nothing.
- `mul` (number, optional): Multiplied in after every addition. Left out, one.

<a id="add-objective"></a>
## `add_objective`

Shows a hidden objective (13 §5.1): it becomes active, its expiry starts and `objective_changed` is raised with `active`. One that is not hidden is left as it is.

`id` may be given directly.

- `id` (string): The objective's id.
- `mission` (int, optional): The number of the mission it is part of; left out, one of the scenario's own.

<a id="add-part"></a>
## `add_part`

Adds a new part of a definition to a body (06 §6.5), on the part `on` in a socket that takes it, or with `inside` inside it, with the organs its definition brings. A part of that name that is gone is replaced. Gives the new part. Refused with `unknown_part`, `no_such_socket`, `socket_refuses`, `no_free_socket`, `part_name_taken`, `too_many_parts`, `bad_amount` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `on` (part?): The part it is joined to.
- `part` (id<body_part>): What kind of part.
- `socket` (string?, optional): The socket it takes. Left out, the first, by name, that would take it.
- `inside` (bool?, optional): Whether it goes inside the part rather than on it.
- `name` (string?, optional): Its name in the body. Left out, its definition's id, numbered if that is taken.
- `side` (string?, optional): Its side label.
- `scale` (real?, optional): Its size relative to the body, above zero. Default 1.

<a id="add-tag"></a>
## `add_tag`

Gives an entity a tag. Raises `tag_changed` if it did not have it.

- `to` (entity): Who is given the tag.
- `tag` (string): The tag: any text.

<a id="add-track"></a>
## `add_track`

Gives a mind a track of someone, or brings the one it has up to date (15 §7.1).

- `who` (entity): The mind.
- `of` (entity): Whom it gains a track of.
- `at` (any, optional): Where it is believed to be: a cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `how` (string, optional): `told` (the default), `inferred` or `carried`.
- `confidence` (real, optional): 0 to 1; 1 if left out.

<a id="add-trait"></a>
## `add_trait`

Gives an entity a trait (06 §5), as every rule gives it. New to it, the trait gains an instance with one stack, and traits of its `group` are removed first; had already, its `stacking` says what happens: `none` nothing, `refresh` its duration starts again, `stack` it gains a stack up to `max` and its duration starts again. The hook `trait_adding` runs first; `trait_added` follows. Returns how many stacks the instance has. Refused with `trait.unknown`, `trait.bad_duration` and by a handler of the hook.

- `to` (entity): Who is given it.
- `trait` (id<trait>): The trait.
- `duration` (real?, optional): How long it lasts this time, in seconds of the entity's own time, above zero. Left out, its definition's `duration`.

<a id="advance-track"></a>
## `advance_track`

Adds to a track's counter; `track_advanced` is raised for each level reached (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `track` (id<track>): Which track.
- `amount` (number): What to add to its counter: not negative.

<a id="anchor-clock"></a>
## `anchor_clock`

Pins an entity's personal clock under a chosen clock, whatever the entity stands in (03 §3.4). An entity with no personal clock is given one at rate 1, which raises `clock_rate_changed`.

- `who` (entity): Whose personal clock.
- `to` (any, optional): What to pin it under: an area that has a clock, a realm, a cell (the clock of that place) or an entity (the clock it is on). Null, or left out, lifts the anchor.

<a id="arrest"></a>
## `arrest`

Catches an entity in flight (02 §15): its body is taken out where it is now and the entity stands there. Raises nothing. Refused for an entity not in flight.

- `what` (entity): Who or what is caught.

<a id="ask-reaction"></a>
## `ask_reaction`

Asks a directly controlled entity how to answer a window it noticed (03 §7.3): a `Reaction` decision listing the reactions that may answer it, each saying whether it would be ready in time and, if it cannot start, why. Time does not move until `React` or `Pass` answers. Gives whether it asked: false for anyone not directly controlled, for one already asked, and where nothing may answer. Refused with `engine:window_closed` or `engine:window_not_noticed`.

- `who` (entity): Who is asked: a directly controlled candidate that noticed the window.
- `window` (window): The window.

<a id="attach-sense"></a>
## `attach_sense`

Gives an entity a sense (15 §4): it sweeps at the sense's interval from now on. Refused for a sense it has already (`perception.has_sense`) or that is not loaded.

- `who` (entity): Who is given it.
- `sense` (string): The sense's id, qualified or bare.

<a id="cancel-action"></a>
## `cancel_action`

Cancels an entity's running actions that match, each in a phase whose `cancel` is true: `on_cancel` runs and `action_cancelled` is raised. A held phase is given up. Gives how many.

- `who` (entity): Whose actions.
- `action` (id<action>, optional): Only actions of this definition.
- `channel` (id<channel>, optional): Only actions holding slots of this channel.
- `tag` (string, optional): Only actions whose definition carries this tag.

<a id="check-stability"></a>
## `check_stability`

Asks for a stability check of a cell and what it holds up (02 §14.2), after the settle delay. What no longer stands falls (`collapse_started`). Refused for a cell not loaded or outside the realm.

- `at` (loc): The cell.

<a id="checkpoint"></a>
## `checkpoint`

Asks the application for a save the player cannot make by hand (13 §9.1), at the next safe point, and raises `checkpoint_made`. It is saved under every saving policy but `none`.

`name` may be given directly.

- `name` (string): The checkpoint's name.

<a id="clear-goal"></a>
## `clear_goal`

Makes a mind give up the goal it holds and think again (09 §17). Gives whether it held one.

- `who` (entity): The character.

<a id="clear-path"></a>
## `clear_path`

Forgets the path the mover is following (06 §11).

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): Whose path.

<a id="clear-plan"></a>
## `clear_plan`

Empties a plan (03 §5.3). Raises `plan_cleared` if it held anything.

- `who` (entity): Whose plan.

<a id="clear-track"></a>
## `clear_track`

Takes a mind's track of someone away. Returns whether there was one.

- `who` (entity): The mind.
- `of` (entity): Whose track it loses.

<a id="close-window"></a>
## `close_window`

Withdraws an opportunity (03 §13): the window closes now, as at its deadline. Gives whether it was open.

- `window` (window): The window.

<a id="close-wound"></a>
## `close_wound`

Closes an open wound: it stops leaking and what it goes through begins to heal (06 §7.3).

`wound` may be given directly.

- `wound` (wound): The wound.

<a id="complete-interaction"></a>
## `complete_interaction`

Ends an interaction its action began (16 §3.4): tests reach and `if` against truth again, runs its `do` and raises `interacted`. The effect that ends the phase of an interaction's action. Refused as `interact` is, but for the hook `interaction_starting`, which ran when the action began.

- `who` (entity): Who does it: a character, or a device acting.
- `target` (any): What it is done to: an element or an entity.
- `interaction` (id<interaction>): The interaction.

<a id="complete-objective"></a>
## `complete_objective`

Settles an active objective as done (13 §5.1): its `on_done` runs and `objective_changed` is raised. An objective that is not active is left as it is. Refused with no game, or no such objective.

`id` may be given directly.

- `id` (string): The objective's id.
- `mission` (int, optional): The number of the mission it is part of; left out, one of the scenario's own.

<a id="create-area"></a>
## `create_area`

Makes an area (02 §8.3): a box from `at` to `to`, every cell within `radius` metres of `at`, or the one cell `at`. Whoever it comes over is told (`area_entered`). Returns the area. Refused for a box in two grids, a kind that does not exist, and a shape larger than the engine allows.

- `at` (loc): A corner of the box, or the middle.
- `to` (loc?, optional): The other corner of a box.
- `radius` (real?, optional): For a round area: the distance in metres, a storey counting three.
- `kind` (id<area_kind>?, optional): Its kind, which gives default tags, variables, clock rate, priority and rules.
- `tags` (list<string>?, optional): Tags, added to its kind's.
- `clock_rate` (real?, optional): The rate of a clock of its own, relative to its realm's.
- `priority` (int?, optional): Which area applies where several overlap.

<a id="create-item"></a>
## `create_item`

Makes `count` items of a definition as one entity (06 §9.1): in a container with `in`, at a cell with `at`, and otherwise out of the world. More than one needs a definition that stacks. Put `in` a container, it is merely inside it: `put_in` stows it. Returns the item. Refused with `item.unknown_def`, `item.bad_count`, `item.not_stackable` and what the kernel refuses of the place.

`def` may be given directly.

- `def` (id<item>): What to make.
- `count` (int?, optional): How many, as one stack. Default 1.
- `at` (loc?, optional): The cell to put it in.
- `in` (entity?, optional): The entity to put it inside. Wins over `at`.

<a id="create-mind"></a>
## `create_mind`

Gives an entity a new mind, awake. Refused for one that has a mind (06 §8.2).

`in` may be given directly.

- `in` (entity): What is given a mind.
- `def` (string, optional): The behaviour profile for the AI layer: the id of a `mind` definition, kept as written.

<a id="damage"></a>
## `damage`

Delivers a packet of damage to one element of a cell, by the rule of 02 §12.2, with the cause it is handed: below the threshold nothing happens; otherwise the element is damaged (`element_damaged`) or destroyed (`element_destroyed`, rubble, and fragments along `dir` if one is given). Returns `unaffected`, `damaged` or `destroyed`. Refused for a cell not loaded or outside the realm, and for a damage type that does not exist.

- `at` (any): The cell, or the element: an element names its own layer.
- `layer` (string?, optional): For a cell: `floor`, `block` or `fixture`. Default `block`.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `energy` (real): Joules delivered.
- `intensity` (real): How concentrated, in pascals (J/m³).
- `dir` (any, optional): The direction of the blow, east, south and up, as a list of three numbers, or something to strike toward. With one, what is destroyed throws fragments.

<a id="damage-part"></a>
## `damage_part`

Adds a share of a whole layer to the damage of one layer of a part, or of each (06 §6.5). No wound is made, and no layer is taken past 254 255ths. Gives null. Refused with `part_missing`, `no_such_layer`, `bad_amount` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `part` (part?): The part.
- `layer` (int?, optional): The layer, 0 for the outermost. Left out, every layer.
- `share` (real): The share of a whole layer, above zero.

<a id="destroy"></a>
## `destroy`

Destroys an element outright, as though damage of a kind had been more than it could take (02 §12.3): it becomes its `on_destroy` state or is removed, its matter is left as rubble, and `element_destroyed` is raised with nothing absorbed. Returns whether there was an element. Refused for a damage type that does not exist and a cell not loaded.

- `of` (element): The element.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage it is destroyed by, as `element_destroyed` reports it.

<a id="destroy-item"></a>
## `destroy_item`

Unmakes an item, with every member of its stack. What it held is first put down where it was; contents never made are never made. Refused with `item.not_an_item`.

`item` may be given directly.

- `item` (entity): The item.

<a id="die"></a>
## `die`

An entity's mind stops driving it for good, after the hook `entity_dying`. Control of it is released; the entity remains (06 §8.3).

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): Who stops.

<a id="disable-channel"></a>
## `disable_channel`

Disables slots of a channel (03 §6.2). Whatever then holds more slots than are enabled is interrupted, newest first, with `engine:action_channel_disabled`.

- `who` (entity): Whose slots.
- `channel` (id<channel>): Of which channel.
- `count` (int, optional): How many slots; one if left out.

<a id="disable-part"></a>
## `disable_part`

Disables a part from outside, whatever its condition, until `restore_part` (06 §6.5).

`part` may be given directly.

- `part` (part): The part.

<a id="drop"></a>
## `drop`

Puts a held thing down where its holder is (06 §9.2): in the holder's cell, or inside whatever encloses the holder. Raises `item_leaving`, then `item_removed` if it was worn, then `item_dropped`. Returns what lies there: the thing, or an equal stack it joined. Refused with `item.not_held` and by a handler of `item_leaving`.

`what` may be given directly.

- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.

<a id="emit-signal"></a>
## `emit_signal`

Gives off a signal (15 §3.2): every observer it reaches receives it, at once or, for a kind with `delay`, when its front arrives. Returns how many observers it was sent to.

- `kind` (string): The signal kind's id, qualified or bare.
- `at` (any): Where it comes from: a cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `strength` (real): How strong it is where it starts.
- `about` (entity, optional): The entity it is about, if any.

<a id="enable-channel"></a>
## `enable_channel`

Enables slots of a channel that were disabled; never more than were.

- `who` (entity): Whose slots.
- `channel` (id<channel>): Of which channel.
- `count` (int, optional): How many slots; one if left out.

<a id="enclose"></a>
## `enclose`

Makes an area of the closed space round a cell (02 §8.3): it fills outward through open cells and, if the space closes within `limit` cells, makes an area over it. Returns the area. Refused, naming a cell it leaks through, for a space that does not close; for a covered start, a fill that reaches unloaded cells, and a limit above 65,536.

- `from` (loc): A cell inside the space.
- `kind` (id<area_kind>?, optional): The kind of area to make.
- `limit` (int?, optional): The most cells it may hold. Default 65,536.

<a id="end-mode"></a>
## `end_mode`

Switches a mode of an ability off (08 §5.4): its trait and its upkeep go together, its `on_end` runs and `mode_ended` follows with `how` `ended`. Returns true. Refused with `ability.not_held`, `ability.mode_unknown`, `ability.mode_off`.

- `who` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `mode` (string): The mode's id within the ability.

<a id="end-scenario"></a>
## `end_scenario`

Ends the game (13 §9.4): raises the hook `scenario_ending`, whose handlers may change `as` or cancel, then `scenario_ended`, and asks the application to end it. Refused with no game, once it has ended, and when a handler cancels.

`as` may be given directly.

- `as` (string): The outcome it names: `won`, `lost`, `escaped`.

<a id="enqueue-action"></a>
## `enqueue_action`

Puts an action at the end of a plan (03 §5.3); it starts when what is before it has and its channels are free.

- `who` (entity): Whose plan.
- `action` (id<action>): The action.
- `with` (map<any>, optional): Its parameters, by name.

<a id="face"></a>
## `face`

Turns an entity with senses to face a place or a direction (15 §4).

- `who` (entity): Who turns.
- `toward` (any): A cell, something that is somewhere, or a number of degrees clockwise from north.

<a id="fail-mission"></a>
## `fail_mission`

Fails an active mission (13 §5.2): its `on_failed` runs and `mission_failed` is raised.

`mission` may be given directly.

- `mission` (int): The mission's number.

<a id="fail-objective"></a>
## `fail_objective`

Settles an active objective as failed (13 §5.1): its `on_failed` runs and `objective_changed` is raised. Refused with no game, or no such objective.

`id` may be given directly.

- `id` (string): The objective's id.
- `mission` (int, optional): The number of the mission it is part of; left out, one of the scenario's own.

<a id="fit"></a>
## `fit`

Fits an item to another (07 §11.5): a magazine, a sight, a muzzle. It is held `fixed` in it, and gives a shot through it its `shot` numbers while it is; taking it into a grasp takes it off. Returns the item. Refused with `ranged.cannot_fit`: none of its tags is in the other's `shot.fits`, or one carrying it is fitted already.

- `what` (entity): The item fitted.
- `into` (entity): The item it is fitted to.

<a id="follow-path"></a>
## `follow_path`

Takes the next step of the path the mover is following, as `step` does (06 §11). A refused step marks the path stale: `plan_path` again.

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): Who steps.

<a id="give"></a>
## `give`

Hands a held thing to another's grasp (06 §9.2): `take` by `to`. Returns what `to` grasps. Refused with `item.not_held` for a thing inside nothing, and as `take` is.

- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.
- `to` (entity): Who takes it: it needs a body.

<a id="graft-part"></a>
## `graft_part`

Attaches a part that came off a body, from this body or another (06 §6.5): the item it left. Its parts keep their names, layers, damage and size, not their wounds; the item is used up. Gives the grafted part. Refused with `not_a_part` and as `add_part` is.

- `item` (entity): The item a part left.
- `on` (part?): The part it is joined to.
- `socket` (string?, optional): The socket it takes. Left out, the first, by name, that would take it.
- `inside` (bool?, optional): Whether it goes inside the part rather than on it.

<a id="grant-ability"></a>
## `grant_ability`

Gives an entity an ability from a rule (08 §3.3): a pact, a lesson, a theft. New to it, it gains an instance at `rank` (or its definition's), watched by its `while`, conferring what it lists if that holds; held already, the rule becomes another source of the one instance and `rank` sets its rank; revoked, it is held again. The hook `ability_granting` runs first; `ability_granted` follows for an ability newly held. Returns the instance. Refused with `ability.unknown`, `ability.bad_rank` and by a handler of the hook.

- `to` (entity): Who is given it.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `rank` (int?, optional): The rank, for an ability with no track. Left out, its definition's.

<a id="heal-part"></a>
## `heal_part`

Takes a share of a whole layer off the damage of every layer of a part. A wound whose layers are whole again is healed (06 §6.5).

`part` may be given directly.

- `part` (part): The part.
- `share` (number): The share of a layer, above zero; 1 makes every layer whole.

<a id="hit"></a>
## `hit`

Applies a hit to a body: the hook `hit_incoming`, then the layers (06 §7). Gives a map of what came of it: `absorbed`, `returned` and `exited` in joules, `destroyed` and `cancelled`.

- `target` (entity): Whose body is hit.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `energy` (number): Joules delivered.
- `intensity` (number): How concentrated the delivery is, in pascals.
- `part` (part, optional): The part it is aimed at. Left out with `height` and `spread`, it lands on one outer part chosen by exposed area.
- `height` (number, optional): The height above the target's footing it arrives at, in metres: it lands on an outer part whose band holds that height.
- `spread` (bool, optional): Whether it is spread over every outer part.
- `area` (number, optional): The area of contact, in square metres. Not used by a spread hit.
- `span` (number, optional): The length of contact across the part, in metres. Not used by a spread hit.
- `dir` (list<number>, optional): The direction it travels in: east, south and up.

<a id="impulse"></a>
## `impulse`

Pushes an entity that is in flight (02 §15): adds an impulse to its body. Refused for an entity not in flight (`world.not_in_world`) or beyond loaded space.

- `what` (entity): Who or what is pushed.
- `j` (any): The impulse in kg·m/s, east, south and up, as a list of three numbers.

<a id="interact"></a>
## `interact`

Does an interaction at once (16 §3.4): checks that the target offers it, that `who` reaches it (raising `interaction_reach`) and that its `if` holds, raises `interaction_starting`, runs its `do` and raises `interacted`. What a device's rules call: an actuator that opens a door. A character does it through an interaction's action, which takes its time. Refused with `interaction.not_offered`, `interaction.out_of_reach`, `interaction.not_now`, `interaction.no_target`, and by a handler of `interaction_starting` with its reason.

- `who` (entity): Who does it: a character, or a device acting.
- `target` (any): What it is done to: an element or an entity.
- `interaction` (id<interaction>): The interaction.

<a id="interrupt"></a>
## `interrupt`

Interrupts an entity's running actions that match, except those in an `uninterruptible` phase: `on_interrupt` runs and `action_interrupted` is raised with `action.interrupted`. Gives how many.

- `who` (entity): Whose actions.
- `action` (id<action>, optional): Only actions of this definition.
- `channel` (id<channel>, optional): Only actions holding slots of this channel.
- `tag` (string, optional): Only actions whose definition carries this tag.

<a id="interrupt-plan"></a>
## `interrupt_plan`

Empties a plan and asks what to do next: a `Free` decision for a directly controlled entity, `decision_needed` for anyone else, whatever is running.

- `who` (entity): Whose plan.

<a id="launch"></a>
## `launch`

Throws an entity that stands in the world (02 §15): it becomes a body in flight with its own mass, volume, cross-section and planes, from the middle of its cell at the height it stands, and the world carries it until it lands. Raises `body_launched`. Refused for an entity not standing in the world (`world.not_in_world`), one already in flight, and one with no mass.

- `what` (entity): Who or what is thrown.
- `vel` (any): Its velocity in m/s, east, south and up, as a list of three numbers.

<a id="load"></a>
## `load`

Loads rounds into a store (07 §11.5), one at a time and in that order: from `from`, a container or a stack of rounds; with none, from whatever `who` carries, at any depth. Only rounds the store takes, and as many as fit, at most `count`. `into` is the store, or a weapon with one fitted. Returns how many were loaded. Refused with `ranged.not_a_store`, and with `ranged.nothing_to_load` or the first refusal of `put_in` when none was.

- `who` (entity?, optional): Who loads, whose carried rounds are taken. Default `self`.
- `into` (entity): The store, or a weapon whose store it fills.
- `from` (entity?, optional): A container to take rounds from, or a stack of rounds.
- `count` (int?, optional): The most to load. Default as many as fit.

<a id="make-notable"></a>
## `make_notable`

Makes an anonymous individual notable, so that it is kept when its tract unloads (06 §12.2).

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): Who is to be remembered.

<a id="materialise-contents"></a>
## `materialise_contents`

Opens a container whose contents have not been made (06 §9.3): makes them from its definition's `contents`, drawn from its own seed, and stows them. Raises `contents_materialised`. Returns what was made: nothing for a container opened before. Refused with `item.not_an_item`.

`container` may be given directly.

- `container` (entity): The container.

<a id="move-to"></a>
## `move_to`

Puts an entity in a cell where it can be: nothing in its way there, room for it, nobody who blocks it. If nothing holds it up there it falls (06 §11).

- `who` (entity): Who is placed.
- `to` (loc): The cell.

<a id="open-window"></a>
## `open_window`

Publishes an opportunity (03 §7.1) that no phase closes: it is offered and noticed as a phase's window is, and closes when its time is over (`window_closed`). Gives the window.

- `kind` (id<window_kind>): Its kind.
- `source` (entity?, optional): Whose doing it is; none for a window no one opened.
- `for` (list<entity>, optional): Those it is aimed at.
- `time` (real): How long it stays open, in seconds of universal time: `"2 s"`.

<a id="plan-path"></a>
## `plan_path`

Plans a path from what the mover believes and keeps it as the path it is following (06 §11). A refusal raises `path_failed`.

- `who` (entity): Who is to go.
- `to` (loc): Where to.
- `max_cost` (number, optional): The dearest path worth having, in metres of travel. No limit if left out.

<a id="pool-add"></a>
## `pool_add`

Adds to a pool, negative to drain, after the hook `pool_changing`. Gives what was in fact added: less where the pool's bounds stopped it (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.
- `amount` (number): What to add; negative to drain.

<a id="pool-rate"></a>
## `pool_rate`

Applies a rate to a pool under a key, replacing the one that key had applied (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `pool` (id<pool>): Which pool.
- `key` (string): The name the rate is applied under.
- `rate` (number, optional): What the pool gains each second of its owner's time; negative to drain. Left out, the rate under this key is removed.

<a id="promote"></a>
## `promote`

Promotes an element to its device entity (02 §5.5) and returns it: the one there already, or a new one bound to the element, with `device_promoted`. Afterwards `target.device` names it, so that something can be put inside it. A device left in its default state with nothing inside is dropped again when something next leaves it or its state is next set, or when the interaction that promoted it ends. Refused for an element whose definition names no device (`device.none`), no element (`device.no_element`), and a cell not loaded.

`of` may be given directly.

- `of` (element): The element.

<a id="put-in"></a>
## `put_in`

Puts a thing into a container (06 §9.2): an item is stowed in its capacity, anything else is enclosed. A container whose contents have not been made is opened first. Raises `item_leaving` and `item_taking`, then `item_taken`. Returns what is in it: the thing, or an equal stack there that it joined. Refused with `item.not_a_container`, `item.not_accepted`, `item.does_not_fit`, what the kernel refuses, and by a handler of either hook.

- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.
- `container` (entity): The container: an item with `holds`.

<a id="put-inside"></a>
## `put_inside`

Puts a thing inside an element's device (02 §5.5, 06 §9.2): promotes the element if it has not been, then `put_in` with the device as the container, so that an item is stowed in its `holds` and anyone else is enclosed, out of the world. Returns what is inside it. A device promoted for nothing is dropped again. Refused as `promote` and `put_in` are.

- `what` (entity): The thing, or whoever hides.
- `into` (element): The element whose device takes it.

<a id="react"></a>
## `react`

Starts a reaction to a window (03 §7.3), cancelling actions of `who` in phases that allow it to make room. Gives whether it started; if it did not, `action_refused` says why: `engine:window_closed`, `engine:window_not_noticed`, `engine:window_noticed_late`, `engine:reaction_not_listed`, `engine:reaction_not_on_behalf`, `engine:reaction_cannot_cancel` or any reason an action is refused.

- `who` (entity): Who reacts: a candidate that noticed the window.
- `window` (window): The window answered: `event.window` of `window_noticed`.
- `action` (id<action>): The reaction: an action whose `reaction_to` lists the window's kind.
- `with` (map<any>, optional): Its parameters, by name; those left out take their defaults, worked out with `$window` bound.

<a id="release"></a>
## `release`

Lets energy go at a place (02 §13): an explosion, a shockwave, a cone of fire, a beam. Raises `release_started` at once and `energy_released` when the front has gone as far as it goes; what it does on the way carries the cause it is handed. Refused for energy not above zero, a damage type that does not exist, a place not loaded, a cone or beam with no direction, a cone's angle not above zero and at most π, a beam with no radius or range.

- `at` (any): Where: a cell, an element's cell, or an entity where it stands.
- `kind` (id<damage_type>): The kind of damage.
- `energy` (real): Joules let go.
- `shape` (string?, optional): `sphere` (the default), `cone` or `beam`.
- `dir` (any, optional): For a cone or a beam: its axis, east, south and up, as a list of three numbers, or something to aim at.
- `half_angle` (real?, optional): For a cone: the angle from its axis to its edge, in radians.
- `radius` (real?, optional): For a beam: how far from its axis it reaches, in metres.
- `range` (real?, optional): For a beam: how far it goes, in metres.
- `burst` (bool?, optional): For a beam: whether what is left where it ends is let go there as a sphere. Default false.
- `speed` (real?, optional): The speed of the front in m/s. Default the speed of sound where it starts.
- `height` (real?, optional): Metres above the base of the cell. Default the middle of the storey, or where an entity stands.

<a id="remember"></a>
## `remember`

A mind remembers something, as inferred (15 §7.1). The least salient memory is forgotten to make room.

- `who` (entity): The mind.
- `event` (string): What happened: an event type or any name.
- `at` (any, optional): Where: a cell, or something that is somewhere.
- `salience` (real, optional): How much it matters, 0 to 1; 0.5 if left out.
- `actor` (entity, optional): Who the mind takes to have done it.

<a id="remove"></a>
## `remove`

Takes a worn item off into its wearer's grasp (06 §9.2): `take` by the wearer. To take it off and put it down, `drop` it. Raises `item_removed`, then `item_taken`. Returns what the wearer grasps. Refused with `item.not_worn`, and as `take` is.

`what` may be given directly.

- `what` (entity): The worn item.

<a id="remove-area"></a>
## `remove_area`

Removes an area (02 §8.3). Whoever was inside it is told (`area_exited`), and its clock goes. Refused for an area that does not exist.

- `area` (area): The area.

<a id="remove-mind"></a>
## `remove_mind`

Removes an entity's mind and discards it, with what was seated in it (06 §8.2).

`from` may be given directly.

- `from` (entity): What loses its mind.

<a id="remove-modifier"></a>
## `remove_modifier`

Removes what was added under a key, to one attribute or to all (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `key` (string): The key the modifiers were added under.
- `attr` (id<attribute>, optional): The one attribute to take them from. Left out, every attribute.

<a id="remove-part"></a>
## `remove_part`

Takes a part off a body with everything on it and in it, and reports it as `part_detached`. The root cannot be taken off (06 §6.5).

`part` may be given directly.

- `part` (part): The part.
- `sever` (bool, optional): True to leave the parts listed as gone, as a hit that severs does; left out, the body simply no longer has them.

<a id="remove-tag"></a>
## `remove_tag`

Takes a tag away from an entity. Raises `tag_changed` if it had it.

- `from` (entity): Who loses the tag.
- `tag` (string): The tag.

<a id="remove-trait"></a>
## `remove_trait`

Removes a trait from an entity, whoever gave it (06 §5): every stack, or with `stacks` that many, taken from its givers in the order they gave it. The hook `trait_removing` runs first; `trait_removed` follows for each giver's instance it touched. Returns how many stacks went: 0 for a trait the entity does not have, which changes nothing. Refused with `trait.unknown`, `trait.bad_stacks` and by a handler of the hook.

- `from` (entity): Whose trait.
- `trait` (id<trait>): The trait.
- `stacks` (int?, optional): How many stacks to take away, at least one. Left out, all of them.

<a id="reopen-wound"></a>
## `reopen_wound`

Opens a closed wound again: it leaks as it did and its time to close starts over (06 §7.3).

`wound` may be given directly.

- `wound` (wound): The wound.

<a id="repair-item"></a>
## `repair_item`

Takes a share of an item's whole capacity off its damage (06 §9.1): 1 mends it entirely. Raises `item_repaired`. An item that is equal again to a stack in the same hold rejoins it. Returns the entity that now holds it. Refused with `item.bad_amount` for a share that is not above zero.

- `item` (entity): The item.
- `share` (real): The share of its capacity to mend, above zero.

<a id="replace-part"></a>
## `replace_part`

Swaps a part's definition (06 §6.5), keeping its name, its place and what is attached to it; its layers are new and its wounds gone. What is on it and no longer fits the new definition's sockets comes off, reported as `part_detached`. Gives null. Refused with `unknown_part`, `socket_refuses`, `part_missing` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `part` (part?): The part.
- `with` (id<body_part>): The new definition.

<a id="restore-checkpoint"></a>
## `restore_checkpoint`

Asks the application to go back to a checkpoint (13 §9.1) at the next safe point. Refused, with `scenario.no_checkpoint`, when there is none of that name or none at all. Carrying memories across is not built.

`name` may be given directly.

- `name` (string, optional): The checkpoint. Left out, the last one made.

<a id="restore-part"></a>
## `restore_part`

Takes back what `disable_part` did: the part works again if its condition allows (06 §6.5).

`part` may be given directly.

- `part` (part): The part.

<a id="revive"></a>
## `revive`

A dead entity's mind drives it again (06 §8.3).

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): Who starts again.

<a id="revoke-ability"></a>
## `revoke_ability`

Takes an ability away from an entity whatever its sources (08 §6.3): its modes end, what it conferred is taken back and `ability_revoked` follows. A trait that lists it does not bring it back while that trait lasts; a rule's `grant_ability` does. The hook `ability_revoking` runs first. Returns whether it was held. Refused with `ability.unknown` and by a handler of the hook.

- `from` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.

<a id="scale-body"></a>
## `scale_body`

Gives a body a new overall size (06 §6.5): every part, its height and its mass go with it. Gives null. Refused with `no_body`, `bad_amount` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `who` (entity): Whose body.
- `scale` (real): Its overall size factor, above zero.

<a id="scale-part"></a>
## `scale_part`

Gives a part a new size relative to its body (06 §6.5): its length, girth and layers go with it, its mass with the cube. Gives null. Refused with `part_missing`, `bad_amount` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `part` (part?): The part.
- `scale` (real): Its size relative to the body, above zero.

<a id="set-attr-base"></a>
## `set_attr_base`

Gives an entity a base of its own for an attribute, in place of the definition's (06 §4.4).

- `who` (entity): Whose stats.
- `attr` (id<attribute>): Which attribute.
- `base` (number, optional): The base of its own; left out, the definition's is given back.

<a id="set-awareness"></a>
## `set_awareness`

Sets an observer's awareness of something through one of its senses, raising what crossing a level raises (15 §5.1).

- `who` (entity): The observer.
- `of` (entity): Whom or what it is aware of.
- `sense` (string): The sense's id, qualified or bare, which the observer must have.
- `level` (real): The level, 0 to 1. 0 forgets the pair.

<a id="set-block"></a>
## `set_block`

Puts a block in a cell, or takes it away (02 §7.2). A block put there starts undamaged; whoever it leaves no room is moved aside (`occupant_displaced`) or walled in (`occupant_entombed`). Raises `element_changed`, and asks for a stability check if a block was removed or weakened. Refused as `set_floor` is.

- `at` (loc): The cell.
- `to` (string?, optional): What to put there, as data writes a state: `def`, `def@material`, `def#state` or `def@material#state`. Null takes what is there away.

<a id="set-body-plan"></a>
## `set_body_plan`

Rebuilds a body from another plan (06 §6.5), keeping each part the new plan names with the same definition, damage and wounds included; what the plan does not map comes off, reported as `part_detached`. Gives null. Refused with `unknown_plan`, `too_many_parts`, `no_body` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `who` (entity): Whose body.
- `plan` (id<body_plan>): The plan.

<a id="set-clock-rate"></a>
## `set_clock_rate`

Changes the rate of an area's or a realm's clock (03 §13). Whoever is inside an area that gains or loses its clock is put on the clock that now applies. Raises `clock_rate_changed`.

- `of` (any): An area or a realm.
- `rate` (real, optional): The rate against the clock above it: zero or more. Null, or left out, takes an area's clock away and is refused for a realm.

<a id="set-color"></a>
## `set_color`

Changes the colour an item carries (06 §9.1), for every member of its stack; null takes it away. Refused with `item.not_an_item`.

- `of` (entity): The item.
- `color` (string?, optional): The colour's name. Null for none.

<a id="set-control"></a>
## `set_control`

Changes who decides for an entity (03 §5.1). Raises `control_changed` if that changes anything; one that comes under direct control with nothing to do is asked what to do.

- `who` (entity): Whose.
- `mode` (string): `none`, `direct` or `delegated`.

<a id="set-driver"></a>
## `set_driver`

Makes one entity act for another's body without moving any mind, after the hook `mind_transferring` (06 §8.2).

- `of` (entity): Whose body is acted for.
- `driver` (entity, optional): Who acts for it. Left out, nobody does.

<a id="set-field"></a>
## `set_field`

Sets the level of a field in a cell outright (02 §16); zero takes it away. Returns the level it had. Refused as `add_field` is.

- `at` (loc): The cell.
- `field` (id<field>): The field.
- `level` (int): The level, 0 to 255.

<a id="set-fixture"></a>
## `set_fixture`

Puts a fixture in a cell, or takes it away (02 §7.2). As `set_block`, with no stability check.

- `at` (loc): The cell.
- `to` (string?, optional): What to put there, as data writes a state: `def`, `def@material`, `def#state` or `def@material#state`. Null takes what is there away.

<a id="set-floor"></a>
## `set_floor`

Puts a floor in a cell, or takes it away (02 §7.2). A floor put there starts undamaged. Raises `element_changed`, and asks for a stability check if a floor was removed or weakened. Refused for a cell that is not loaded or outside the realm, and for a state that names nothing (`world.unknown_state`).

- `at` (loc): The cell.
- `to` (string?, optional): What to put there, as data writes a state: `def`, `def@material`, `def#state` or `def@material#state`. Null takes what is there away.

<a id="set-goal"></a>
## `set_goal`

Makes a mind take up a goal now, stopping what the character is doing where it can (09 §17). It is held until it is done, fails or `clear_goal`, whatever else scores higher.

- `who` (entity): The character.
- `goal` (id<goal>): The goal.
- `about` (any, optional): What it is about: an entity, as the mind perceives it, or a cell. Left out, nothing.

<a id="set-home"></a>
## `set_home`

Says where a mind belongs: what `self.home` reads.

- `who` (entity): The character.
- `at` (loc): The cell it belongs at.

<a id="set-layer"></a>
## `set_layer`

Changes what a layer of a part is made of, how thick it is, or both (06 §6.5). A layer keeps its damage. Gives null. Refused with `no_such_layer`, `unknown_material`, `part_missing`, `bad_amount` and by a handler of `body_changing`.

- `part` (part?): The part.
- `layer` (int?, optional): The layer, 0 for the outermost. Left out, every layer.
- `material` (id<material>?, optional): What it is to be made of. Left out, as it is.
- `thickness` (real?, optional): How thick it is to be, in metres, above zero. Left out, as it is.

<a id="set-material"></a>
## `set_material`

Makes an element of another material (02 §7.2): it keeps its definition, its state and its damage. Raises `element_changed`; a block or floor asks for a stability check. Refused where there is no element (`world.no_element`), for a material that does not exist, and for a cell not loaded.

- `of` (element): The element.
- `material` (id<material>): What it is to be made of.

<a id="set-mind-def"></a>
## `set_mind_def`

Makes a character think by another `mind` definition (09 §17): it gives up the goal it holds and thinks again.

- `who` (entity): The character, which must have a mind.
- `mind` (id<mind>): The `mind` definition it thinks by from now on.

<a id="set-movement"></a>
## `set_movement`

Says which ways of moving an entity has (06 §11).

- `who` (entity): Whose ways of moving.
- `modes` (list<id<movement>>): The ways of moving it has, in the order they are tried. Empty: the definitions flagged `default`, for a creature.

<a id="set-posture"></a>
## `set_posture`

Puts an entity in a posture (06 §11.1). The hook `posture_changing` may cancel; `posture_changed` follows.

- `who` (entity): Whose posture.
- `posture` (id<posture>, optional): The posture. Left out or null: none.

<a id="set-rank"></a>
## `set_rank`

Sets the rank of an ability with no track (08 §4.1): what applies from a rank is brought into line, modes above it end, and `rank_changed` follows if it changed. Returns the rank before. Refused with `ability.not_held`, `ability.rank_from_track` and `ability.bad_rank`.

- `who` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `rank` (int): The rank, from 0 to 10,000.

<a id="set-stance"></a>
## `set_stance`

Makes a mind hold someone hostile or feared, or neither (09 §3.4). Relations (15 §9) will take its place.

- `who` (entity): The character whose mind takes the stance.
- `of` (entity): Whom: the stance is kept toward what the mind perceives them as.
- `stance` (string): `hostile`, `feared` or `none`.

<a id="set-state"></a>
## `set_state`

Puts an element into another of its states (16 §3.5): a door open or shut, a lamp on or off. It keeps its definition, its material and its damage. Raises `element_changed`; whoever a state that blocks leaves no room is moved aside. Refused where there is no element, for a state its definition does not declare (`world.unknown_state`), and for a cell not loaded.

- `of` (element): The element.
- `state` (string): The name of one of its definition's states, or its bits as a number written as text.

<a id="set-time-rate"></a>
## `set_time_rate`

Gives an entity a clock of its own at a rate, changes the rate of the one it has, or takes it away (03 §3.5). Everything about the entity runs on it. Raises `clock_rate_changed`.

- `who` (entity): Whose personal clock.
- `rate` (real, optional): Its rate against the clock of where the entity is: zero or more. Null, or left out, takes the personal clock away, and any anchor with it.

<a id="shoot"></a>
## `shoot`

Fires a shot (07 §11.1): from where `from` stands, at a height, toward `at` or along `dir`, with dispersion of `spread` drawn from the stream `shots`. With a `store`, each of `count` shots takes the store's next round and launches its projectile, as many as the round says, with the round's energy times the weapon's efficiency; with none, `count` projectiles of `projectile`. Each flies as a body in flight (02 §15) and strikes what it meets, or with `speed` `instant` is cast as a ray that strikes at once (07 §11.3). Raises `projectile_fired` for each; spends each round and leaves its casing. Returns how many projectiles were fired. Refused with `ranged.empty`, `ranged.no_projectile`, `ranged.no_energy`, `ranged.no_aim`, `ranged.not_in_world`, `ranged.not_a_store`, `ranged.too_many` and `ranged.bad_number`, having changed nothing.

- `from` (entity?, optional): Who shoots. Default `self`.
- `at` (any, optional): What it is aimed at: an entity, at the height of `part` or `height`, or the middle of its body; a cell, at `height` above its floor or level; or a point, a list of three numbers in metres. One of `at` and `dir`.
- `dir` (any, optional): The direction it is aimed along, east, south and up, as a list of three numbers.
- `part` (part?, optional): The part of the entity aimed at: the shot is aimed at the middle of its band.
- `height` (real?, optional): Metres above the footing of the entity, or the floor of the cell, it is aimed at; and above the shooter's footing it leaves from. Default: at a part's band, or the middle of a body; it leaves at 0.8 of the shooter's height.
- `projectile` (id<projectile>?, optional): What it fires, for a shot with no store, or in place of what the store's rounds name.
- `store` (entity?, optional): The store its rounds come from: a magazine, a quiver, or a weapon with one fitted.
- `with` (entity?, optional): The weapon it is fired with: its `shot` numbers, and those of what is fitted to it, give the spread, efficiency, noise and flash the effect leaves out.
- `energy` (real?, optional): Joules each projectile leaves with, in place of the round's times the efficiency.
- `speed` (any, optional): Metres a second each projectile leaves at, in place of what its energy gives; or `instant`, for a ray.
- `spread` (real?, optional): Radians: the standard deviation of each of its two angles of dispersion. Default the weapon's, else none.
- `count` (int?, optional): How many shots: rounds from the store, or projectiles. Default 1; at most `shoot.max_count`.
- `noise` (real?, optional): How loud, for `projectile_fired`. Default the weapon's, else 0.
- `flash` (real?, optional): How bright, for `projectile_fired`. Default the weapon's, else 0.
- `lob` (bool?, optional): Whether it is sent along the lower arc that comes down on the aim point under gravity, not straight at it. Default false.
- `range` (real?, optional): For an instant shot: how far the ray goes, in metres. Default `shoot.instant_range`.
- `window` (any, optional): The kind of reaction window it opens for whoever it is aimed at (07 §11.2). Offered to nobody until reaction windows are built.

<a id="spawn"></a>
## `spawn`

Makes an entity from templates and puts it in a place (06 §10.3). Gives the entity made.

- `template` (id<template>): The first template: a species, say.
- `at` (loc, optional): The cell to put it in.
- `in` (entity, optional): The entity to put it inside, if not `at` a cell. Left out with `at`, it is made out of the world.
- `also` (list<id<template>>, optional): More templates, applied after the first in order.
- `random` (bool, optional): True to make a random selection for every choice; left out, each takes its default.
- `seed` (int, optional): What random selections are drawn from. Left out, 0.
- `anonymous` (bool, optional): True to make it an anonymous individual of a population (06 §12.2).

<a id="split"></a>
## `split`

Splits `count` members off a stack as an entity of their own, in the same place and hold (06 §9.1). Raises `item_split`. Returns the piece. Refused with `item.bad_count` unless at least one goes and one stays.

- `item` (entity): The stack.
- `count` (int): How many to split off.

<a id="start-action"></a>
## `start_action`

Starts an action now, as the `Act` command does (03 §6.6). Gives whether it started; if it did not, `action_refused` says why.

- `who` (entity): Who acts.
- `action` (id<action>): The action.
- `with` (map<any>, optional): Its parameters, by name; those left out take their defaults.

<a id="start-mission"></a>
## `start_mission`

Starts a mission (13 §5.2): it is recorded with its parameters, its objectives that wait for nothing are shown and `mission_started` is raised. Gives the mission's number. Refused for a mission that is not loaded, parameters it does not have or lacks, and with no game.

`mission` may be given directly.

- `mission` (string): The mission definition: a qualified id, or a bare name.
- `taker` (entity, optional): Who takes it on. Left out, the character the player plays.
- `with` (map<any>, optional): Its parameters by name.

<a id="start-mode"></a>
## `start_mode`

Switches a mode of an ability on (08 §5.4): what switching costs is taken, its trait given and its upkeep applied together, its `on_start` run; `mode_started` follows. It ends when switched off, when its upkeep runs a pool dry, or when the ability goes dormant or is lost. Returns true. Refused with `ability.not_held`, `ability.dormant`, `ability.rank_too_low`, `ability.mode_unknown`, `ability.mode_on`, `ability.upkeep`, `ability.cost_short`.

- `who` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `mode` (string): The mode's id within the ability.

<a id="step"></a>
## `step`

Takes one step to the cell next to the mover, checked against the world as it is now (06 §11). Takes no time itself: the action waits `self.step_time(dir)`. A refusal raises `step_refused`.

- `who` (entity): Who steps.
- `dir` (string): Which way: `north`, `north_east`, `east`, `south_east`, `south`, `south_west`, `west`, `north_west`, `up` or `down`.
- `drop` (bool, optional): Whether to step off where there is nothing to stand on, and fall. False if left out.

<a id="stow"></a>
## `stow`

Puts a thing into the first container `who` wears or grasps that would take it, in order of id (06 §9.2): `put_in` that container. Returns what is stowed. Refused with `item.no_container` if none would.

- `who` (entity): Whose containers.
- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.

<a id="take"></a>
## `take`

Takes a thing into a grasp of `who` (06 §9.2): picks it up, draws it from a pack, takes it from another's hand, takes it off if `who` wears it. It occupies the slots its `grip` names on the working parts of `who`'s body. Raises `item_leaving` and `item_taking`, then `item_taken`. Returns what is grasped: the thing, or an equal stack in `who`'s grasp that it joined. Refused with `item.no_grip`, `item.no_body`, `item.no_free_grasp`, what the kernel refuses, and by a handler of either hook.

- `who` (entity): The creature that holds or wears it: it needs a body.
- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.

<a id="take-control"></a>
## `take_control`

Gives the player direct control of a character (13 §13): it joins the party, those of the party that can no longer act are counted fallen, and the application is asked to show it.

`who` may be given directly.

- `who` (entity): The character.

<a id="take-out"></a>
## `take_out`

Takes a thing out of the container it is stowed in or enclosed by (06 §9.2): into the grasp of `to` as `take` does, or with no `to` to where the container is, as `drop` does. Returns where it went. Refused with `item.not_contained`, and as `take` or `drop` is.

- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.
- `to` (entity?, optional): Who takes it into a grasp. Null to put it where the container is.

<a id="think"></a>
## `think`

Makes a mind think at the next batch (09 §3.3). Refused for a character that thinks by no `mind` definition.

- `who` (entity): The character whose mind thinks.

<a id="throw"></a>
## `throw`

Throws an item `who` holds (07 §11.1): it leaves the hand and flies as a body that is the item, with its own mass and cross-section, from where `who` stands toward `at` or along `dir`, and strikes what it meets with its surface named `surface`, through the same delivery as a projectile's; with none, with a blunt blow. Raises `thrown`. Refused with `ranged.not_held`, `ranged.no_surface`, `ranged.no_energy`, `ranged.no_aim`, `ranged.not_in_world` and `ranged.bad_number`.

- `who` (entity?, optional): Who throws. Default `self`.
- `what` (entity): The item thrown: one `who` holds.
- `at` (any, optional): What it is aimed at, as for `shoot`.
- `dir` (any, optional): The direction it is aimed along, as a list of three numbers.
- `part` (part?, optional): The part of the entity aimed at.
- `height` (real?, optional): Metres above the footing of the entity, or the floor of the cell, it is aimed at.
- `energy` (real?, optional): Joules it leaves the hand with.
- `speed` (real?, optional): Metres a second it leaves the hand at, in place of what its energy gives.
- `spread` (real?, optional): Radians of dispersion, as for `shoot`. Default none.
- `surface` (string?, optional): The id of the item's surface it strikes with. Default none: a blunt blow.
- `lob` (bool?, optional): Whether it is sent along the arc that comes down on the aim point. Default false.

<a id="transfer-mind"></a>
## `transfer_mind`

Moves a mind to another entity, with the attributes, pools and tracks seated in it and the control mode, after the hook `mind_transferring` (06 §8.2).

- `from` (entity): Whose mind moves.
- `to` (entity): Where it goes.
- `swap` (bool, optional): True to let a mind that `to` has go the other way; left out, `to` must have none.

<a id="use-ability"></a>
## `use_ability`

Uses an ability (08 §5): starts the action one of its grants makes available, through the action runtime, with its cost taken in full and its cooldown started, after the hook `ability_using`. Returns whether the action started; when it did not, `ability_refused` says why (`ability.not_held`, `ability.dormant`, `ability.rank_too_low`, `ability.cooling_down`, `ability.condition`, `ability.cost_short`, `ability.cost_source_gone`, `ability.items_short`, a refusal of the action runtime, or a handler's).

- `who` (entity): Whose ability.
- `ability` (id<ability>): The ability.
- `action` (id<action>?, optional): The action of the grant. Left out, the ability's only grant.
- `params` (any, optional): The action's parameters, a map by name. The grant's own `params` stand in for any of the same name.

<a id="wait"></a>
## `wait`

Occupies an entity doing nothing (03 §13). When the time is over it is free, and asked what to do next.

- `who` (entity): Who waits.
- `time` (real): How long, in seconds of its own time: `"2 s"`.

<a id="wear"></a>
## `wear`

Puts an item on `who` (06 §9.2): it covers the outer parts its `wear` selects, at its layers, and is a layer for hits on them. One member of a stack is split off and worn. Raises `item_leaving` and `item_taking`, then `item_worn`. Returns what is worn. Refused with `item.not_wearable`, `item.no_body`, `item.no_part_to_wear_on`, `item.layer_taken`, what the kernel refuses, and by a handler of either hook.

- `who` (entity): The creature that holds or wears it: it needs a body.
- `what` (entity): The thing, wherever it is.
